title: They laughed first.
paragraphs: They laughed first.

Not with quiet doubt…
—but loud, public, humiliating laughter.
“What are these feeble Jews doing?” (Nehemiah 4:2)
That’s how it started.

Before the threats.
Before the lies.
Before the traps.
It always starts with mockery.

And if you’ve ever tried to rebuild your life—
you know that voice.

“Look at you… trying again?”
“After everything you’ve done?”
“You really think God can use you?”
That’s Sanballat talking.
That’s Tobiah whispering.
That’s Geshem circling.
Listen carefully.

Because this is not just ancient history written in Nehemiah 2–6.
This is a mirror.

You finally decide to rebuild your prayer life—
suddenly distraction multiplies.

You commit to purity—
temptation intensifies.

You say, “Lord, I’m coming back”—
and hell doesn’t stay silent.
Why?
Because rebuilding threatens the enemy.

Ruins don’t scare him.
Restoration does.

Nehemiah didn’t walk into comfort.
He walked into conflict.

God gave the vision…
but opposition showed up immediately.
And here’s the part most people miss—

Opposition is not proof you’re out of God’s will.
It’s often proof you’re right in the center of it.

Sanballat used ridicule.
Tobiah used alliances and inside influence (Nehemiah 6:17–19).
Geshem used false narratives and public accusation (Nehemiah 6:6).

Different strategies.
Same goal:
Stop the work.

Not destroy Jerusalem—
just delay it.
Distract it.
Discourage it.

Because if he can’t destroy you,
he’ll try to drain you.
And it almost worked.

The people grew tired.
The rubble felt overwhelming (Nehemiah 4:10).
Sound familiar?

“Ang dami pang aayusin…”
“Parang hindi ko kaya…”
“Maybe I should just stop…”

That moment right there—
that’s where destinies either collapse…
or get forged.
But Nehemiah did something powerful.

He didn’t deny the fear.
He redirected it.
“Do not be afraid of them. Remember the Lord, who is great and awesome…” (Nehemiah 4:14)

Not “remember your strength.”
Not “believe in yourself.”
Remember the Lord.

Because rebuilding is not sustained by hype.
It is sustained by revelation.
Then came the strategy.

Half the men worked.
Half stood guard.

Builders with swords.
Laborers with alert eyes.
“Those who carried burdens were loaded in such a way that each labored on the work with one hand and held his weapon with the other.” (Nehemiah 4:17)
Catch this—

You don’t pause your calling to fight battles.
You build while you fight.

You pray while you work.
You stay alert while you serve.
This is spiritual maturity.
Then the enemy changed tactics.

If intimidation doesn’t work…
try invitation.
“Come, let us meet together…” (Nehemiah 6:2)

Looks harmless.
Sounds reasonable.
But Nehemiah saw through it.
“They intended to harm me.”
So he answered with one of the coldest, most focused lines in Scripture:
“I am doing a great work and I cannot come down.” (Nehemiah 6:3)

Not emotional.
Not defensive.
Focused.
Let that sink in.

Every distraction loses power
when your calling becomes clear.
And then… the lies.

False prophets.
Fake letters.
Reputation attacks.
They tried to make Nehemiah look like the villain.

Because if they couldn’t stop the work externally,
they would try to corrupt it internally.
But truth has a way of outlasting noise.
Always.
And here’s the victory line most people rush past:
“So the wall was finished…” (Nehemiah 6:15)
Finished.

Despite mockery.
Despite fear.
Despite fatigue.
Despite lies.
Finished.

What God starts—
He finishes through surrendered people.
Now pause.
Because this is where the Gospel steps in.

Nehemiah rebuilt broken walls.
But he couldn’t rebuild broken hearts.
That required Someone greater.

Jesus didn’t come with a trowel—
He came with a cross.

He didn’t face mockery from three men—
He faced it from crowds.
“He saved others; he cannot save himself.” (Matthew 27:42)
Sound familiar?

Same spirit.
Different century.
But Jesus didn’t come down from His “wall.”
He stayed.

Through nails.
Through shame.
Through silence.

And when it looked like the enemy had won—
the stone rolled away.

Not just from a tomb…
but from every life willing to be rebuilt.
So here you are.

Maybe halfway through your wall.
Maybe staring at rubble.
Maybe tired.
Hear me—

You are not crazy for rebuilding.
You are not weak for struggling.
You are not disqualified because of your past.

If God called you to it—
He will carry you through it.
But you must decide:

Will you come down…
or will you stay on the wall?

🔥 Pray like it depends on God.
🔥 Work like He gave you the assignment.
🔥 Stand like the fight is real—because it is.

And when the voices rise again—
because they will—

Answer them with Scripture.
Answer them with focus.
Answer them with faith.

“I am doing a great work…
and I cannot come down.”
If this spoke to your fight, don’t keep it to yourself.
Drop a 🔥 if you’re rebuilding.

Because somebody out there is one voice away from quitting—
and this might be the one that keeps them on the wall.
We tell the stories that shame tried to erase.
